subject: Production: DeepValley VPC - P95 spike, 502s and throughput drop
messages:
From: Anna Rivera <anna.rivera@deepvalley.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Production: DeepValley VPC - sudden P95 spike and 502s

Hi Michael,

We started seeing a production regression this morning on our private VPC deployment (tenant: deepvalley-prod). Key symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~2.1s, a sharp increase in 502/5xx responses (from 0.2% to ~6.8%), and end-to-end throughput dropped ~40%. This started around 07:45 PST and is persisting.

Our engineers see a flood of backend timeouts and GPU process restarts in the node logs. We attached a short sample of request traces (deepvalley-error-sample.log). We haven't changed model variant intentionally in the last week; traffic profile did increase slightly but not enough to explain the severity.

This is customer-impacting for our immediate appointments workflow. Can you please escalate and advise on immediate mitigations? If we need a live call, we can join ASAP.

Thanks,
Anna Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
DeepValley Health

Thanks for the ping — I started a brief triage against the sample logs Anna attached. Early observations and an interim mitigation plan: 

Observations:
- Spike correlates with a surge of long-context requests (tokens per request shifted +3x starting 07:40) which caused increased KV cache churn and higher decode latency for hot shards.
- We see repeated KV cache evictions in the runtime logs (evict_count high) and occasional kernel-level retries in the GPU driver logs. Not classic OOMs but persistent process restarts on 2 of 8 nodes.
- The batch window that runs at 07:30 in DeepValley’s pipeline appears to have increased batch size (they added a new telemetry enrichment) and that pushed hot-sequence density to the same hot shards.

Interim mitigations (low-risk, test-first):
1) Temporarily increase KV cache allocation:
   - runtime config: caching.kv_size -> +30%
   - restart one replica at a time (rolling)
2) Add a short-term decode fallback to an older quantized variant for very long requests:
   - route requests > 2k tokens to gpt-4-alt-q4_0-hosted (degrades perf but reduces 5xx)
3) Rate-limit the nightly batch injection at the edge (throttle to 50% of current for 30m)
4) If restarts continue, collect full GPU driver logs and kernel trace (we’ll ask ops for sudo access to /var/log/nvidia/*)

I’ve prepared a small patch to the runbook for this scenario and attached it (deepvalley-runbook-diff.patch). If team confirms we can apply mitigation (1) and (3) now, I’ll coordinate a rolling deploy and monitor.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Laura / Irene — forwarding summary from the front-line triage for exec visibility. TL;DR: p95 up to ~2.1s, 5xx spike ~6-7%, throughput -40%, likely root cause is sudden long-context batch traffic that caused KV cache thrash and hot-shard overload. Two of eight nodes have had process restarts; we’re not seeing persistent GPU OOMs yet.

Immediate asks:
- Approval to enable temporary hosted-fallback routing for the tenant (will add cost but reduces customer impact)
- Decision on SLA credit if we cannot fully remediate within 48 hours (we may need to offer service credit and prioritize kernel patch backport)
- War-room at 09:00 PT to align on public statement and next steps (we’ll invite DeepValley and product/infra leads)

I’m coordinating mitigation actions (Marissa’s plan). Anna — Michael here, can you confirm the batch job owner and whether you can throttle that pipeline for 30 minutes while we stabilize?

—Michael
